news.title: Copper Princesses to face China in World Cup warm-up
news.lede: Zambia’s Copper Princesses will face China in an international friendly as part of their final preparations for the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The match will be played in Rabat on 9 October, eight days before the tournament gets underway. Football Association of Zambia (FAZ) General Secretary Charles Chakatazya said the fixture would give Zambia valuable preparation against Asian opposition ahead of their Group D meeting with Japan. “As part of the Copper Princesses’ preparations for the World Cup, we have secured a high-profile friendly against China to give the girls a taste of Asian football,” Chakatazya said.

news.title: No bitterness over World Cup omission, Azmoun says after Iran recall
news.lede: FILE PHOTO: Soccer Football - World Cup - AFC Qualifiers - Third Round - Group A - Iran v United Arab Emirates - Azadi Sports Complex, Tehran, Iran - March 20, 2025 Iran's Sardar Azmoun in action with United Arab Emirates' Kouame Kouadio Majid Asgaripour/WANA (West Asia News Agency) via REUTERS/File Photo. Sept 22 - Iran striker Sardar Azmoun said he bears no bitterness over being left out of the squad for the World Cup and that his recall to the national team on Monday stirred the same joy he experienced with his first call-up. Azmoun is his country's second-leading scorer of all time with 57 goals in 91 games but was left out of the squad for the World Cup in North America with state news agency IRNA saying he was injured.

news.title: West Cork footballers represent Ireland at Transplant World Cup
news.lede: THREE West Cork transplant recipients - including the team manager who was given just two months to live in 2007 - will return from representing Ireland at the Transplant Football World Cup in Frankfurt this weekend. The players were part of a Transport Sport Ireland team of ten at the tournament where 15 national teams of organ transplant recipients from across the world celebrated the gift of life, athletic resilience, and the power of organ donation. The team includes manager Mike Keohane from Rosscarbery, Val Weblin from Leap and Patrick O’Driscoll from Aghiohill. Mike was told in 2007 that he had just two months to live without a transplant.

news.title: Spain secure World Cup-winning boss Luis de la Fuente to massive long-term contract extension
news.lede: Luis de la Fuente has officially committed his long-term future to the Spanish national team after putting pen to paper on a bumper new contract extension. The RFEF have moved quickly to secure the services of the man who led La Roja to global dominance, ensuring stability for the next decade of international football. The Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) has taken the unprecedented step of securing De la Fuente’s future for the next six years, rewarding the veteran coach for his historic success on the international stage. Following a meeting at the Ciudad del Futbol in Las Rozas, the governing body confirmed that the 65-year-old has agreed to a contract that will run until 2032.

news.title: Falconets Are Back! Nigeria’s U-20 Girls Return Home After World Cup Battle
news.lede: Nigeria’s U-20 Women’s National Team, the Falconets, have arrived back in Abuja following their campaign at the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland. The team returned to Nigeria after representing the country on the global stage, bringing their latest international campaign to a close. Sports247 reports that the Falconets earned their place in the knockout stages after producing a strong group-stage performance before advancing to the quarter-finals. Nigeria’s campaign included an impressive 3-0 victory over England in the Round of 16, a result that secured their passage into the last eight of the competition.

news.title: Spain locks in World Cup-winning coach through 2032
news.lede: MADRID (AP): Spain has agreed to extend the contract of World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente until 2032. The Spanish football federation said yesterday that its board of directors unanimously approved the contract extension. The new deal will keep De la Fuente at the helm through the 2030 World Cup, which Spain will co-host with Morocco and Portugal, as well as the 2028 and 2032 European Championships. “We are looking for a project built on stability and trust,” Federation President Rafael Louzán said.

news.title: CommBank Junior Matildas squad revealed for historic FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2026
news.lede: CommBank Junior Matildas Head Coach Michael Cooper has named the 21-player squad that will make history at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup Morocco 2026™, where Australia is set to compete at the tournament for the first time. Australia secured its historic qualification at the AFC U-17 Women’s Asian Cup China 2026™ with a 2-0 quarter-final victory over Vietnam, before the team went on to finish fourth at the tournament. The squad retains the core group from its successful AFC U-17 Women’s Asian Cup campaign, reflecting the continuity and progress of a team that has developed together throughout the cycle. Sienna Calvanese and Rubi Sullivan come into the playing group, adding further depth ahead of the tournament.

news.title: Africa’s Moment? The Battle To Host Football’s 2030 World Cup Final
news.lede: Football’s ultimate fixture awaits its scheduling. The first major triumph of the 2030 World Cup will come long before the kick-off of the tournament, to be co-hosted by Morocco, Portugal and Spain. It will be the decision on which of the three countries gets the prestige of hosting the final, a call that world football’s governing body, FIFA, will make. Exactly when is unclear, and each passing month only heightens the tension ahead of the announcement.
